e: 'a different ___' needs a noun: frequency (a radio channel). Frequently is the adverb.

q: From the mud on his boots, it was ______ that he had just come in from the field.
e: 'It was evident that' = it was clear that. Evidence is the noun.

q: Both of my parents believed that a good ______ was the key to a successful career.
e: 'a good ___' needs a noun: education. Educational is the adjective.

q: Since the new speed limit was introduced, there has been a ______ drop in accidents on base.
e: An adjective describes the noun 'drop': noticeable (keep the e after c).

q: Military working dogs are trained to show complete ______ to their handlers.
e: 'show complete ___' needs a noun: obedience. Obedient is the adjective.

q: The two countries have signed an ______ to hold joint training exercises every summer.
e: 'signed an ___' needs a noun: agreement. Agreeable means pleasant.

q: Wearing a reflective belt is ______ for anyone running on base roads after dark.
e: Obligatory = required by the rules. Obliged is used for people (you are obliged to ...).

q: The new helmet is ______ light, weighing about half as much as the old model.
e: An adverb modifies the adjective 'light': comparatively (= when compared with others).

q: Soldiers who live off base receive a monthly housing ______ to help pay their rent.
e: A noun is needed: allowance (= money given regularly for a purpose).

q: When I explained that my father was in the hospital, my supervisor was very ______ and gave me the week off.
e: After 'was very' we need an adjective: sympathetic (= showing understanding and kindness).

q: With twelve years of competition experience, Sergeant Lee is ______ the best marksman in the battalion.
e: Arguably (adverb) = it can be said, with good reason, that ...

q: Thanks to the ______ of local businesses, every child on base received a holiday gift.
e: 'the ___ of' needs a noun: generosity. Generous is the adjective.

q: The families were very ______ of all the help the volunteers gave them during the move.
e: 'be appreciative of' = be grateful for. 'Appreciated' cannot be followed by 'of' here.

q: Heavy rain had flooded the main road through the valley overnight; ______, the convoy had to take a much longer route and arrived six hours late.
e: A linking adverb is needed after the semicolon: consequently (= as a result).

q: In his farewell speech, the general thanked his staff for their ______ during a difficult year.
e: 'their ___' needs a noun: loyalty. Loyal is the adjective.

q: The investigation report was highly ______ of the way the evacuation had been handled.
e: 'be critical of' = say what is wrong with something. Criticism is the noun.

q: The instructor spoke ______ even though the recruit had made a serious mistake.
e: An adverb describes how he spoke: calmly.

q: There are several ______ between the two rifles, but the newer model is much lighter.
e: 'several' needs a plural noun: similarities.

q: A good scout must be ______; she notices every footprint and broken branch along the trail.
e: After 'must be' we need an adjective: observant (= quick to notice things).

q: With the new software, staff can ______ track the location of every vehicle in the fleet.
e: An adverb goes between 'can' and the verb: can easily track.

q: Your ______ has improved a lot since you started the evening language course.
e: The noun is pronunciation, spelled without the 'o' of pronounce (pro-NUN-ciation).

q: My neighbors have been ______ for fifteen years and have moved eight times.
e: 'have been married for' (adjective) gives the length of the marriage.

q: Regular exercise and a balanced diet are essential for good ______.
e: 'for good ___' needs a noun: health. Healthy is the adjective.

q: Your passport must remain ______ for at least six months after you arrive.
e: After the linking verb 'remain' use an adjective: valid. Validity is the noun.

q: It has been a real ______ to work with such a professional team.
e: 'a real ___' needs a noun: pleasure. Pleasant and pleasing are adjectives.

q: She spent most of her ______ on Army bases in Texas and Germany.
e: 'most of her ___' needs a noun: childhood (= the time when you are a child).

q: Light vehicles give the unit greater ______ in mountainous terrain.
e: 'give ... greater ___' needs a noun: mobility (= ability to move easily).

q: Throughout the course, the instructors placed great ______ on weapon safety.
e: 'place emphasis on' uses the noun emphasis; emphasize is the verb.

q: Given the ______ of the situation, a medical team was flown in by helicopter.
e: 'the ___ of' needs a noun: urgency. Urgent is the adjective.

q: Thanks to his ______, the young private finally passed the swim test on his fifth attempt.
e: After 'his' we need a noun: persistence (= continuing despite difficulty).

q: Lack of sleep can seriously ______ a pilot's ability to judge distance and speed.
e: Affect is the verb (= have an influence on); effect is usually the noun (= a result).

q: Check that none of the cargo straps are ______ before the truck leaves the motor pool.
e: Loose (adjective, rhymes with 'goose') = not tight or not firmly fixed; lose is the verb (lose your keys); loss is the noun.

q: Could you ______ me your car on Saturday? Mine is still in the shop.
e: Lend = let someone use something of yours (lend me your car); borrow = take and use something that belongs to someone else (borrow your car).

q: Since the new gym opened, attendance at morning workouts has ______ by almost a third.
e: Rise / rose / risen has no object (attendance has risen); raise needs an object (raise prices); arise = come into existence (a problem arises).

q: Too exhausted to unpack, Private Moore ______ on his bunk with his boots still on.
e: Lie (= be in a flat position): lie / lay / lain. Lay (= put something down) needs an object: lay / laid / laid. Lied is the past of lie (= say something false).

q: The town's ______ survival depends heavily on the Air Force base just outside it.
e: Economic = related to the economy, trade and jobs; economical = not wasting money or fuel (an economical car).

q: These files contain ______ information and must be locked in the safe at the end of each day.
e: Sensitive = secret or needing careful handling (also: easily hurt); sensible = reasonable and practical. Careful: French 'sensible' means 'sensitive'.

q: Investigators said the ______ cause of the fire was a faulty heater in the storage room.
e: Principal (adjective) = main, most important; principle (noun) = a basic rule or belief.

q: During the inspection, the general paid the cooks a ______ on how clean the kitchen was.
e: Pay someone a compliment = praise them; a complement is something that completes or goes well with something else.

q: The truck was ______ at a red light when the bus hit it from behind.
e: Stationary (adjective) = not moving; stationery (noun) = paper, envelopes and other office supplies. Memory aid: stationEry = papEr.

q: It took the recruits from Alaska several weeks to ______ to the summer heat in Texas.
e: Adapt to = change to suit new conditions; adopt = start to use a plan or idea, or take a child into your family; adept = skilled.

q: All ______ entering the hangar must sign the log and wear a visible badge.
e: Personnel (stress on the last syllable) = the people who work for an organization; personal = private, belonging to one person.

q: After the security check, passengers should ______ directly to Gate 14 for boarding.
e: Proceed = go forward or continue; precede = come before something in time or order.

q: From the captain's long silence, we ______ that our request had been denied.
e: The listener infers (= reaches a conclusion from evidence); the speaker implies (= suggests without saying it directly).

q: Before you ship your household goods overseas, ______ them for their full value.
e: Insure = buy insurance against loss or damage; ensure = make sure something happens; assure = tell someone confidently that something is true.

q: Two masked men ______ a gas station on Route 9 late last night and escaped in a stolen pickup.
e: You rob a person or place (rob a gas station, rob a bank); you steal a thing (steal money from a gas station).

q: Please ______ me to call the motor pool before noon, or I will certainly forget.
e: Remind someone to do something = make them remember it; remember and recall happen in your own memory and do not take 'me to do'.

q: His ______ would not let him keep the wallet he had found in the parking lot.
e: Conscience (noun) = your inner sense of right and wrong; conscious (adjective) = awake and aware; conscientious = careful and hard-working.

q: The base commander has *allocated* two extra classrooms to the language program this semester.
o: lent for a short time only
e: Allocate = officially give or set aside something (money, space, time) for a particular purpose.

q: The last line of the order was *ambiguous*, so two platoons ended up at different landing zones.
o: open to more than one meaning
e: Ambiguous = unclear because it can be understood in more than one way.

q: Good planners *anticipate* problems with the weather and pack extra rain gear before every exercise.
o: deal with only after they occur
e: Anticipate = expect something and prepare for it before it happens.

q: The staff felt the new parking assignments were *arbitrary* and asked the office to explain how the spaces had been chosen.
e: Arbitrary = based on chance or personal choice, not on a reason or system.

q: After the storm, engineers arrived to *assess* the damage to the hangar roof.
e: Assess = examine something carefully to judge its size, value or quality.

q: The delay in this month's pay statements was *attributed to* a software error at the finance office.
e: Attribute something to = say or believe that it is the result of something.

q: Even after twenty hours without sleep, the captain gave a *coherent* account of the accident.
e: Coherent = clear, logical and easy to follow.

q: The airline will *compensate* passengers whose bags arrive more than two days late.
e: Compensate = give someone money or something else to make up for a loss, injury or trouble.

q: The clerk spent two days *compiling* a list of every vehicle that needs new tires.
e: Compile = collect information from different places and put it together in a list, report or book.

q: New employees receive a *comprehensive* guide to the company's safety rules during their first week.
e: Comprehensive = complete, covering all or nearly all details. Do not confuse it with comprehensible (= easy to understand).

q: Keep your summary *concise*; the general rarely reads past the first page of any report.
o: full of exact numbers and dates
e: Concise = giving the necessary information in few words.

q: Budget *constraints* mean that the unit will not get new computers until next year.
e: A constraint is something that limits or restricts what you can do.

q: Do you know the *criteria* the selection board uses to choose candidates for flight school?
o: people who make the final choice
e: Criteria (plural of criterion) = the standards used to judge or decide something.

q: Accurate weather data is *crucial* to the safety of every training flight.
e: Crucial = extremely important, because other things depend on it.

q: The doctor said the recruit's diet was *deficient* in iron, which explained why he was always tired.
e: Deficient in something = not having enough of it.

q: The pain in his knee gradually *diminished* after a week of rest and ice.
e: Diminish = become smaller, weaker or less.

q: Whether you can leave early on Friday is entirely at the supervisor's *discretion*.
e: At someone's discretion = according to their own judgment. (Discretion can also mean keeping secrets, but not here.)

q: A power failure *disrupted* classes at the language school for most of the morning.
e: Disrupt = interrupt something and stop it from continuing normally.

q: This year's class of interpreters is the most *diverse* the school has ever had.
e: Diverse = including many different types of people or things.

q: Several new problems *emerged* during the second week of testing the software.
e: Emerge = appear or become known, especially after being hidden.

q: The new night-vision goggles greatly *enhance* a driver's ability to see in the dark.
e: Enhance = improve the quality, value or strength of something.

q: Engineers say a bridge across the river is *feasible*, but it would take three years to build.
e: Feasible = possible and practical to do.

q: Fuel prices *fluctuate* so much that it is hard to plan the transportation budget.
e: Fluctuate = change often and irregularly, going up and down.

q: Heavy snow *hampered* the search for the two missing hikers.
e: Hamper = make it difficult for someone to do something or for something to make progress.

q: The researchers tested their *hypothesis* by comparing two groups of soldiers over six months.
e: A hypothesis is an idea or explanation that has not been proven yet and must be tested.

q: The company offers a cash *incentive* to employees who suggest ways to save energy.
e: Incentive = something, often money, that encourages people to do something.

q: Some risk is *inherent* in parachute training, no matter how careful the instructors are.
e: Inherent = existing as a natural, basic part of something.

q: Last spring, the hospital *initiated* a program to help soldiers stop smoking.
e: Initiate = start something, such as a plan, process or program.

q: Drivers are *liable* for any damage caused to government vehicles through careless use.
e: Liable for = legally responsible for something, and possibly required to pay for it.

q: Planting a row of trees along the runway helped *mitigate* the noise for nearby homes.
e: Mitigate = make something bad less serious or harmful.

q: The difference in price between the two radios is *negligible*, so choose the one that is easier to use.
e: Negligible = so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering.

q: If you will be absent from formation, *notify* the duty desk no later than 0530.
e: Notify = tell someone officially about something.

q: The higher cost of the new boots is *offset* by the fact that they last twice as long.
e: Offset = balance one thing against another so that its effect is reduced or canceled.

q: In any rescue operation, the safety of the crew is *paramount*.
e: Paramount = more important than anything else.

q: Please keep your questions *pertinent* to today's topic; we have only thirty minutes.
e: Pertinent = directly related to the subject being discussed.

q: *Preliminary* results suggest that the new boots reduce foot injuries by about a third.
e: Preliminary = coming before the main or final part; early and not yet complete.

q: A valid driver's license is a *prerequisite* for the forklift operator course.
e: Prerequisite = something that is required before something else can happen.

q: *Prospective* students can visit the campus on Saturdays and talk to the instructors.
e: Prospective = likely or expected to become something in the future (prospective students, buyers, employees).

q: Nurses must follow the hospital's *protocol* for handling patients with a high fever.
e: Protocol = a set of official rules or steps for doing something.

q: The memo explains the *rationale* behind moving morning formation to 0630.
e: Rationale = the reasons or logic behind a decision or action.

q: The editor marked the second paragraph as *redundant* and deleted it from the final report.
e: Redundant = not needed because it repeats something or is more than necessary. (In British English it can also mean 'dismissed from a job'.)

q: The team spent another month *refining* the software before releasing it to the units.
e: Refine = improve something by making small changes.

q: Auditors will *scrutinize* every receipt from the deployment before approving the final budget.
e: Scrutinize = examine something very carefully and in detail.

q: Since the incident in March, security checks at the airport have become far more *stringent*.
e: Stringent = very strict and difficult to satisfy (stringent rules, checks, standards).

q: The new online system should *streamline* the process of applying for leave.
e: Streamline = make a process simpler and more efficient.

q: The first test was canceled, but all *subsequent* tests were completed without any problems.
e: Subsequent = coming after something else; later.

q: Checking thousands of serial numbers by hand is a *tedious* job.
e: Tedious = long, slow and boring.

q: The cleaning contract may be *terminated* if the company misses three deadlines.
e: Terminate = end something officially (a contract, an agreement, a job).

q: Next spring, the battalion will *undertake* a major review of its training program.
e: Undertake = accept and start doing a task or responsibility.

q: Before takeoff, the crew chief must *verify* that all access panels are securely closed.
e: Verify = check that something is true or correct.

q: Without a reliable supply of spare parts, the plan to keep the old trucks running is not *viable*.
e: Viable = able to work or succeed in practice.

q: Computers that are never updated are *vulnerable* to cyber attacks.
e: Vulnerable to = easily hurt, damaged or attacked by.

q: The community college agreed to *waive* the application fee for military families.
e: Waive = officially decide not to demand a payment or apply a rule.

q: The new dining facility can *accommodate* up to 400 soldiers at a time.
e: Accommodate = have enough space for a number of people.

q: The supply office is in the building *adjacent* to the chapel.
e: Adjacent to = next to or very near.

q: Several doctors *advocate* shorter shifts for medical staff as a way to reduce mistakes.
e: Advocate (verb) = publicly support or recommend an idea or policy.

q: The medicine should *alleviate* the pain, but it will not cure the infection.
e: Alleviate = make pain or a problem less severe.

q: The staff had to *amend* the travel orders when the departure date changed.
e: Amend = make changes to a document, law or plan to correct or improve it.

q: Every employee receives a performance *appraisal* at the end of the year.
e: Appraisal = a formal judgment of how well someone is doing their job (a performance review).

q: At the hearing, the driver *asserted* that the brakes had failed before the collision.
e: Assert = state something firmly and confidently.

q: Because of the computer outage, the finance office now has a *backlog* of 300 travel claims.
e: Backlog = an amount of work that should already have been done and is still waiting.

q: This year's fitness scores will serve as a *benchmark* for measuring progress.
e: Benchmark = a standard or point of reference used to measure or compare other things.

q: The study was criticized for *bias*, since it was paid for by the company that makes the drug.
e: Bias = an unfair preference for or against someone or something.

q: The change-of-command ceremony will *commence* at 1400 in front of headquarters.
e: Commence = begin (formal).

q: The Army plans to *consolidate* three small supply depots into one large facility.
e: Consolidate = combine several things into one larger, more effective unit.

q: The sale of the house is *contingent on* the buyer getting a bank loan.
e: Contingent on = depending on something that may or may not happen.

q: Pilots must not *deviate* from the approved flight plan without permission from air traffic control.
e: Deviate from = do something different from what is planned or expected.

q: The reporter was accused of *distorting* the general's comments to make them sound more critical.
e: Distort = change facts or words so that they give a false meaning.

q: Months of delays have *eroded* the team's confidence in the new contractor.
e: Erode = gradually reduce or destroy something, as water slowly wears away rock.

q: Could you *expedite* my passport application? I'm deploying in two weeks.
e: Expedite = make a process happen faster.

q: An experienced interpreter will *facilitate* communication between the two delegations.
e: Facilitate = make an action or process easier.

q: The suspect was not very *forthcoming* about where he had spent the night.
e: Forthcoming about something = willing to give information. It can also mean 'about to happen', but not here.

q: After several fights in town, the base commander *imposed* a curfew on all junior enlisted soldiers.
e: Impose = officially force a rule, tax or punishment on people.

q: Soldiers who return library books late may *incur* a small fine.
e: Incur = become responsible for a cost, or suffer something unpleasant, because of your own actions.

q: The workshop gave us real *insight* into how the logistics system actually works.
e: Insight into something = a clear, deep understanding of it.

q: The radio worked well at first, but later the signal became *intermittent*.
e: Intermittent = stopping and starting again; not continuous.

q: The missing generator on the equipment list was simply an *oversight* by the supply clerk.
e: Oversight = a mistake made because you did not notice something. (It can also mean 'supervision', but not here.)

q: Since nobody called back, I *presumed* that the meeting was still on.
e: Presume = believe something is true without being sure; assume.

q: Back injuries are especially *prevalent* among truck drivers and warehouse workers.
e: Prevalent = common or widespread in a particular group or place.

q: Our new manager takes a *proactive* approach to safety problems in the warehouse.
e: Proactive = acting early to prevent a problem instead of waiting for it to happen.

q: If the headaches *recur*, make another appointment with your doctor.
e: Recur = happen again.

q: The position offers attractive *remuneration*, including a housing allowance.
e: Remuneration = money and benefits paid for work (formal).

q: Technicians managed to *retrieve* most of the files from the damaged laptop.
e: Retrieve = get something back, such as data or an object.

q: After the new regulation came out, the instructors had to *revise* their lesson plans.
e: Revise = change something to correct or improve it. (In British English it can also mean 'study for an exam'.)

q: Repairing the hangar roof falls outside the *scope* of this contract.
e: Scope = the range of things that a contract, project or subject deals with.

q: The lease *stipulates* that tenants may not keep pets in the apartment.
e: Stipulate = state clearly that something must be done, especially in a contract or rule.

q: Investigators could not *substantiate* the claim that fuel had been stolen from the depot.
e: Substantiate = provide evidence to prove that something is true.

q: After the exercise, the company returned its *surplus* ammunition to the depot.
e: Surplus = more than is needed; extra.

q: The new training program has produced *tangible* results: qualification scores rose by 15 percent.
e: Tangible = real and clear enough to be seen or measured.

q: The new commander promised a more *transparent* process for approving leave requests.
e: Transparent (of a process) = open and honest, so people can see how decisions are made.

q: Constant public criticism can *undermine* a young soldier's self-confidence.
e: Undermine = gradually make something weaker or less effective.

q: The flood caused *unprecedented* damage to the base, closing it for a month.
e: Unprecedented = never having happened before.

q: Sergeant Diaz is a *versatile* mechanic who would be valuable in any motor pool.
e: Versatile = able to do many different things or be used in many ways.

q: The clerk *inadvertently* sent the confidential file to the wrong office.
e: Inadvertently = without intending to; by accident.

q: The two men who *allegedly* sold stolen night-vision goggles online will appear in court next week.
e: Allegedly = according to what people say, although it has not been proven.

q: Commanders are held *accountable* for the safety and welfare of their soldiers.
e: Accountable = responsible for something and expected to explain your actions.

q: After checking the logbook, the sergeant *conceded* that he had made an error.
e: Concede = admit, often unwillingly, that something is true.

q: Rather than wait for new trucks, the colonel took a *pragmatic* approach and repaired the old ones.
e: Pragmatic = dealing with problems in a practical, realistic way.

q: The decision to promote Sergeant Ruiz was *unanimous*, which pleased the whole platoon.
e: Unanimous = agreed by everyone in a group.

q: Engineers came up with a *novel* way to purify water using only solar power.
e: Novel (adjective) = new and different from anything known before. (As a noun, a novel is a book.)
